stories.title: Missouri county drops land sale bid near golf course after protests
stories.summary: Jackson County in Missouri cancelled its request for bids on public land along the Blue River Parkway on November 9 after residents and conservation groups protested the proposed sale. The land has more than eight miles of volunteer-built trails used for hiking and mountain biking. Residents have called for stronger legal protection against future development.

stories.title: 'Warrants urgent attention': SC flags vehicular pollution in Delhi-NCR, seeks action plan
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has mandated that Delhi and three adjacent states intensify measures to combat vehicle emissions. Officials are tasked with reporting on the implementation of laws governing aging and non-compliant vehicles. With rising pollution levels in the National Capital Region, the court emphasized the need for inter-state collaboration on vehicle management and stricter adherence to emission standards. The matter will be reviewed again on November 23.

stories.title: Over 2,000 teachers, students face political persecution in Bangladesh: Report
stories.summary: Since August 2024, over 2,000 students and teachers have reportedly faced politically motivated persecution across Bangladesh. The persecution includes academic exclusion, physical attacks, and criminal proceedings targeting individuals linked to the Bangladesh Awami League. Numerous teachers have experienced exclusion from professional activities, physical assaults, and legal issues. JusticeMakers Bangladesh has called for independent investigations into these reported abuses.

stories.title: Russia's last major independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts down after 33 years
stories.summary: Novaya Gazeta, an independent newspaper critical of the Kremlin, has shut down its Moscow office after three decades. The closure came as a result of mounting government pressure and sustained restrictions on independent media. Journalists mourned the loss of their office while recalling the legacy of their investigative work. Some staff members have relocated abroad and continue reporting under a new publication called Novaya Gazeta Europe.

stories.title: Business drainage changes flood neighbour's home; court cuts damages to $102,000
stories.summary: A Michigan business's drainage changes sent excess rainwater onto a neighbouring property, causing years of flooding and damage to the house and garage. An appeals court revised the homeowner's $170,000 award to $102,000, while upholding $50,000 in emotional distress damages under the nuisance claim.

stories.title: California teens collect 22,000 sports balls in 24 hours for recycling
Rubio warned Trump about Nvidia CEO's Chinese 'spy' affair months ago. Did he ignore it?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed confidence in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang regarding allegations of ties to a Chinese spy. Trump stated he believes Huang was unaware of the alleged spy's identity during an FBI investigation. Rubio's memo on Huang's relationships surfaced before Trump's visit to Beijing, indicating prior knowledge of the situation. The FBI is scrutinizing the implications on national security concerning Nvidia's technology and partnerships.

stories.title: 'I'd quake in my seat': Sonia Gandhi recalls Indira Gandhi's temper, early days as bride in memoir
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, offers an intimate account of Indira Gandhi’s temper, recalling how staff were made to stand in corners, a senior Congress leader ordered to face a wall and others ignored for days. Sonia also describes Rajiv’s reassurance during her mother-in-law’s outbursts, Indira’s domestic routines, love for sarees and photographs, and how grandchildren gradually softened her temperament.

stories.title: Charity shop worker wins £600,000 inheritance battle after murder accusation
After 30 historic wall stones were stolen, UK councillor hid an AirTag in one; police tracked the thief
stories.summary: Determined to protect an ancient wall from persistent thefts, an English mayor cleverly employed an Apple AirTag embedded in one of the coping stones. This initiative ultimately directed police to a thief in Wigan, who confessed to the charges. The recovered stones, estimated at £7,000, have revitalized community spirit, allowing local residents to rally together and restore this historic structure.

stories.title: Idris Elba backs £500,000 UK creative careers programme for 400 youths
High Pollution Alert Issued: Sadiq Khan warns of very high PM2.5; experts seek burn alerts
stories.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan issued a high air pollution alert for the capital urging residents to take precautions. Vulnerable groups were particularly advised to minimize their exposure to polluted air, following high pollution levels. Government monitoring indicated that numerous locations exceeded healthy particulate matter levels due to weather conditions and celebrations. Experts suggested that domestic burning and transportation significantly contribute to air quality issues.

stories.title: After 800 years with one family, 9,500-acre UK estate bought for wildlife with 25,000 donors' help
stories.summary: The Rothbury Estate in Northumberland has successfully been bought for nature conservation, thanks to the generous contributions of over 25,000 supporters from across 50 countries, amassing nearly £30 million. The Wildlife Trusts and Northumberland Wildlife Trust will oversee restoration efforts, plan a nature corridor, and engage with local farmers to align conservation with farming. This purchase heralds a fresh chapter of conservation initiatives and community involvement.

stories.title: US evacuates aircraft from UK air base after Iran threat: Report
What made Sonia Gandhi turn down PM post after UPA’s 2004 victory? Memoir revisits moment
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi reveals her thoughts in her memoir about declining the prime minister role after the UPA's victory. She describes her inner voice guiding her decision and her conversation with Rahul. Gandhi highlights why she chose Manmohan Singh for the position, noting his integrity and governance experience. Her memoir also covers her personal journey, including significant tragedies and cultural adjustments after moving to India.

stories.title: Atacama Desert: Where ancient life reveals the secrets of our planet’s beginnings
stories.summary: In the unforgiving Atacama Desert, ancient stromatolites stand as a testament to early life on Earth and how microbes can adapt to extreme conditions. Researchers are exploring the resilience of microorganisms in this arid environment, revealing insights that might help us understand the possibilities of life on Mars. These findings emphasize how organisms can not only survive but thrive in harsh settings, raising intriguing questions about extraterrestrial existence.

stories.title: Turning trash into treasure with oyster recycling: Alabama's oyster shell recycling program supports local fisheries and habitats
stories.summary: Since 2016, Alabama’s oyster shell recycling program has successfully collected over 31 million shells, contributing to the restoration of an impressive 120.1 acres of oyster habitats in coastal waters. Local restaurants play a key role by properly disposing of their used shells. This initiative not only bolsters marine life and local fisheries but also encourages student involvement in learning about oyster ecology and its vital impact on the ecosystem.

stories.title: Iran war, cost of living drag Trump’s approval rating near career low: Survey
stories.summary: Donald Trump's approval rating stands at 32 per cent, close to his lowest in recent years. Concerns about the cost of living have significantly affected his standing among voters. The Republican Party experienced losses in both chambers of Congress during the midterm elections. Trump has taken action to address immigration, which resonates more positively with his supporters compared to his economic policies.

stories.title: Psychology says Americans who never leave their home state score slightly higher on psychopathy
stories.summary: A recent investigation into American adults revealed intriguing links between childhood residence and personality traits. Individuals who remained in their home state exhibited marginally higher scores in psychopathy. This may stem from their stable relationships and self-serving tendencies. Interestingly, those with psychopathic characteristics were more inclined to settle in urban areas experiencing elevated crime rates. Future studies must delve deeper into how mobility influences personality evolution.

stories.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028 as judge rejects defence's push for 2029
stories.summary: Tyler Robinson, implicated in the assassination of Charlie Kirk, will begin trial in June 2028. The judge aimed to balance the interests of both the defense and Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk. Prosecutors originally sought an earlier trial start, highlighting the family's desire for swift justice. Robinson's lawyers are preparing a substantial defense, examining extensive evidence and potentially seeking a change of venue.

stories.title: Hegseth unfazed by impeachment push, defends Trump's Iran war as 'necessary'
India, US plan joint crackdown on transnational drug cartels, synthetic drug trade
stories.summary: Top security officials from India and the US gathered in New Delhi to address narcotics syndicates. The discussions focused on establishing a framework to combat synthetic drug flows and secure supply chains. NCB Director General Anurag Garg emphasized a network-centric enforcement model to target cartels and facilitators. Both nations endorsed operational milestones, including initiatives to prevent the diversion of synthetic drug precursors.

stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang loses $7.4bn in 30 minutes, drops 2 spots in Forbes rich list
stories.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang faced a notable drop in net worth, tumbling from $162.2 billion to $154.7 billion, following revelations of an ongoing investigation into his supposed involvement with a Chinese spy. The resulting unrest caused Nvidia's shares to plunge by more than 7%, raising alarms about its market stability as broader questions emerge regarding Nokia's dealings in China and their national security ramifications.

stories.title: Three workers killed during water tank maintenance at Tata iPhone parts factory in Tamil Nadu
Hasina seeks passport, Dhaka calls it political stunt & seeks extradition
stories.summary: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has requested a new passport from the Bangladesh High Commission. The request aims to facilitate her planned return to Bangladesh after two years in exile. Bangladesh authorities have labeled the request a political stunt and emphasized her extradition due to criminal convictions. Indian officials have stated that the extradition matter should be handled through existing legal processes.

stories.title: Diwali as US federal holiday? 19 lawmakers back fresh push
stories.summary: A group of Indian-American lawmakers supports legislation to establish Diwali as a federal holiday in the United States. Congresswoman Grace Meng leads the initiative alongside 14 other representatives advocating for the recognition of Diwali. This legislation aims to promote cultural awareness and inclusion among diverse communities. The festival represents significant values across various religious groups and cultures, uniting people.

stories.title: 'Global capital for Sanatan pilgrimage': Akhilesh's big Ayodhya promise ahead of 2027 UP polls
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has articulated a bold vision to elevate Ayodhya as the ultimate hub for Sanatan pilgrimage on a global scale. He stressed the importance of honest temple management and top-notch infrastructure to rejuvenate devotees' trust. Additionally, Yadav has committed to tackling local economic challenges and safeguarding the interests of traditional boatmen.

stories.title: Robbie Williams gives his $40 million Florida mansion a rock-star makeover
Paris Hilton's former Beverly Park home seeks $159,000 a month in rent
Defamation Case Moves Ahead: Kai Cenat says lawsuit enters new phase; McDonald’s livestream clash revives RaKai claims
stories.summary: Kai Cenat has confirmed that his defamation lawsuit against former friend Reggie is moving forward after a McDonald's employee confronted him over allegations involving streamer RaKai. The unexpected exchange happened during his GTA streaming marathon. Kai revealed that his legal team had completed the first stage of the case and was preparing for the next, while expressing frustration over facing the accusations in everyday situations.

stories.title: Massachusetts neighbours ordered to pay $3.7 million after 18-year dispute over oceanfront home construction
stories.summary: Margaret Reichenbach and her husband encountered relentless challenges from their neighbors throughout their home construction project in Massachusetts. After a prolonged legal struggle, they secured a $3.7 million verdict for damages. The Massachusetts Appeals Court affirmed the ruling, citing ample evidence of harassment and intrusion. The Reichenbachs' victory also includes a permanent injunction against further neighbor harassment, finally allowing them peace in their home.

stories.title: Rufus Wainwright lists his $2.3 million Spanish-style Laurel Canyon cottage
Princess Diana's private cottage preserved as her former retreat goes on sale
Ahead of peace talks, Zelenskyy seeks PM Modi's help on ceasefire
stories.summary: Asks For More Steps On Food, Energy Security

stories.title: Paul McCartney's Scottish farm inspired Mull of Kintyre after Beatlemania
Fearing winter polls, Ladakh political parties, social bodies plan protests
Massachusetts neighbours lose appeal over $3.7 million verdict for disrupting couple's home construction
stories.summary: In the divorce proceedings between Vernon and Nichole McIntosh, the court mandated a substantial division of assets following Vernon's misappropriation of funds. Nichole is awarded 55 percent of the marital estate, amounting to over $138,000. The trial established that Vernon hid and mismanaged marital assets during the divorce. Properties purchased during their marriage will be sold, with net proceeds evenly distributed. Vernon must also cover Nichole's attorney fees.

stories.title: The Weeknd bought $50M Florida waterfront mansion with private superyacht dock
Chinese nationals stream from poor localities of Dhaka, claim those are in Delhi: Report
SC: Govt has wide powers to compulsorily retire staffer, improve efficiency
stories.summary: Bona fide appraisal, P 13

stories.summary: No AQI Data From Several Air Monitoring Stns

stories.title: Texas appeals court overturns tenant's $250,000 award over defective legal notice to landlord
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court has overturned a significant $250,000 default judgment that was previously granted to a tenant due to flaws in the service documentation. Lavender Apartments LLC contested the validity of the delivery records, claiming they did not adhere to Texas legal standards. As the court found the required service was inadequately demonstrated, the case will go back for additional litigation and examination in the trial court.

stories.title: Alice Huang boasted about Nvidia AI chip access to investors, told them Alibaba would be a client for the project
Utah court backs family's claim to disputed farmland after 1965 fence outweighs neighbour's survey
stories.summary: A Utah family successfully upheld its legal rights to a disputed piece of farmland after a court ruling. The Christiansen Family Trust contested boundary claims made by Haas Land & Livestock, which purchased neighboring property. The property dispute centered around a fence built in 1965 that marked the boundary. The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed earlier decisions favoring the Christiansens' long-accepted boundary.

stories.title: Now, Cong-led Keralam govt follows Karnataka on 'ethanol test'
stories.summary: Those Creating Controversies For Political Purposes Will Have To Face Consequences: Union Minister

stories.title: Adult vaccination remains low; elderly miss cover against flu and shingles
Lawyers' boycott makes man stay in jail despite bail
Prince Harry exits BetterUp chief role after 5 years on $1 million salary, takes senior adviser post
stories.summary: Prince Harry has stepped down as chief impact officer at BetterUp after five years, moving into a senior adviser role at the US-based mental health and coaching company. The Duke of Sussex reportedly earned $1 million annually during his tenure. The development comes weeks after his return to the UK with Meghan Markle and their children, drawing attention to his professional plans.

stories.title: JD Vance says a lot of infighting, reshuffling going on, people asking if No 2 has what it takes to lead. Then he clarifies he is talking about Ohio State Buckeyes
Ohio residents push data center ban as $5bn Amazon project faces November 10 hearing
stories.summary: Residents in Butler County are rallying against the proposed Amazon data center, voicing worries over possible water shortages, noise pollution, and pollution from backup generators. Local zoning authorities have suggested prohibiting data centers in St. Clair Township, where this project is slated to occur. A crucial public hearing is set to address these issues alongside zoning matters. Recent trends show rising voter favor for restrictions on similar undertakings across Ohio.

stories.title: Diwali is 'Eid of joy', says Kharge; Congress insulting Sanatan culture: BJP
US court rejects malpractice claim over lawyer's missed deadline to correct $100,000 divorce debt error
stories.summary: In a recent ruling, an Arizona appeals court upheld a decision to dismiss a woman's malpractice claim against her ex-attorney. The court concluded she suffered no direct financial loss from the attorney's missed deadline, despite a $200,000 error in the divorce decree regarding familial debt. It was established that the obligation to pay the debt remained unchanged and fully enforceable.

stories.title: 19 runners hospitalized after 'unusual symptoms' at California half-marathon; heat exhaustion might be a reason as Santa Barbara temperatures reached 86 degree Fahrenheit
Michael Jackson's iconic stage glove sells for €113,737 at French auction
Unions dismiss France's 24-euro minimum wage increase
Oregon couple in their 70s win over $8 million after firms foreclose on home they still lived in
stories.summary: An Oregon couple in their 70s have been awarded more than $8 million after a jury found companies liable for unlawfully foreclosing on their home while they were still living in it. The Salem couple had also been denied more than $175,000 left over from the foreclosure sale, which took place in 2022. The jury found that the companies had carried out unlawful trade practices and financially abused the elderly homeowners.

stories.title: Meet Leo Toake, 16, who turned potato peels into weedkiller and restored 15 acres in New Jersey
stories.summary: At just 16 years old, Leo Toake from New Jersey is on a mission to create a revolutionary herbicide sourced from food scraps. Through his nonprofit, Re:Imagine Inc., he's mobilized over 70 volunteers for habitat restoration and invasive species removal. Early trials of Toake's S.A.F.E. clearly show an 82.5% effectiveness against Japanese stilt grass, all while repurposing over 500 pounds of food waste and contributing to a cleaner environment.

stories.title: Kublai Khan’s warship sank in 1281; 745 years later, dice reveal how its crew spent breaks
stories.summary: Archaeologists recently found gaming pieces and dice from a Mongol invasion shipwreck near Takashima Island. These discoveries suggest that sailors engaged in leisure activities during voyages. The ship may measure around 30 metres, potentially the largest of three identified wrecks. Other artefacts discovered nearby include food containers and tools indicative of daily life aboard the ship.

stories.title: Bihar govt bans firecrackers, private boat operations near ghats ahead of Chhath Puja
Delhi Police issues notice to Mamata Banerjee as witness in 2013 protest case
Residents raise $30,000 to bring first grocery store to Alabama neighbourhood in 70 years
stories.summary: After nearly 70 years without a grocery store, Birmingham's Fountain Heights neighbourhood has opened the We All Eat Market. Developed by a local farming cooperative, the $1 million project received $30,000 in grassroots contributions and $150,000 from the city. The market will sell locally grown food, support small farmers and offer discounts to eligible customers.

stories.title: Mona Vale beachfront home fetches record $29 million
stories.summary: A Mona Vale beachfront house recently set a new record by selling for A$29 million in a private sale. The property was previously owned by McDonald's Australia's chief executive and sold for A$7.65 million in 2014. The sale was conducted discreetly without public marketing, ensuring privacy for the owners. The previous record for Mona Vale was A$13.5 million, established in October 2025.

stories.title: 'Anybody believe this was honest?' Trump revives fraud claims after midterm results
Norway’s largest Viking hoard yields rare King Olaf coin not found in country since 1924
stories.summary: A rare coin minted during King Olaf Haraldsson's reign around 1025 has been identified in Norway's Morstad Viking hoard. It is only the second coin of this type found in Norway, the previous one dating back to 1924. The coin also offers clues about the king's use of Christian symbols and its circulation in commercial transactions.

stories.title: Kentucky court keeps father 500 feet from home despite sole ownership claim after wife's death
stories.summary: A Kentucky court has upheld a key decision safeguarding the welfare of two boys by ruling against their father's attempt to rescind protective orders. Although he is the property owner, the court has ordered him to maintain a 500-foot separation from his home. This ruling, following the untimely death of the boys' mother in 2025, emphasizes the priority given to their security over the father's interests.

stories.title: Amateur prospector finds 1.2-kg gold nugget worth A$150,000 in Australia
stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, a hobbyist prospector unearthed a significant gold nugget weighing 1,218 grams in New South Wales. With approximately 940 grams of pure gold, its value is estimated between A$150,000 and A$200,000. The Tibooburra area continues to draw gold seekers and tourists, with this nugget serving as a testament to the dedication and perseverance required in the thrilling quest for gold.

stories.title: $180,000 Bitcoin, Pokemon cards feature in North Carolina divorce appeal
stories.summary: A North Carolina appeals court upheld a divorce court's valuation of three Bitcoin at $180,000, Pokemon cards at $1,800 and its unequal division of marital assets. However, it overturned a $15,261.40 attorney’s fee award and an order requiring the husband to pay the entire forensic accountant’s bill, citing missing findings needed to establish the reasonableness of the fees.

stories.title: 'Scrap Rs 500 notes': CM Naidu seeks to phase out big currency to curb corruption
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu advocates for the abolition of Rs 500 and other high-value banknotes to combat corruption and promote a shift to digital transactions, which he believes is vital for economic enhancement. The recent local election results revealed a strong tilt toward the National Democratic Alliance, especially in urban regions, indicating a robust affirmation of democratic ideals and effective governance across Andhra Pradesh.

stories.title: ‘There is only the United States of America’: Erika Kirk slams Abdul El-Sayed’s ‘Arab America’ remark after historic Senate win
Canada has protected more than 81,400 hectares of Ontario taiga forest and peatlands
stories.summary: A significant investment of $64 million is underway to safeguard over 81,400 hectares of taiga forests and peatlands in Ontario. This project focuses on preserving habitats for wildlife, including vulnerable species such as the red-headed woodpecker and the bobolink. It represents Canada's commitment to conserving 30 percent of its lands and waters by 2030 through a collaborative effort involving various organizations, government entities, and private donors.

stories.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual assault
'There is an old saying': BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari explains her 'firecrackers cure illness' remark, apologises
Idaho reconnected 8 acres of floodplain and built 2,000 feet of side channels
stories.summary: Warm Springs Preserve in Ketchum is currently undergoing significant habitat restoration, aimed at reviving local ecosystems. The initiative includes reconnecting floodplains and building new channels to support aquatic species. An enhanced irrigation system is projected to conserve roughly 50 million gallons of water annually. Furthermore, the project will introduce accessible trails and improved public facilities for the community, marking a commendable step towards better environmental management and habitat preservation.

stories.title: After surveys found only dead oil beetles in 2022 and 2025, volunteers discovered larvae
stories.summary: Exciting news from Pembrokeshire, Wales: conservationists have unearthed short necked oil beetle larvae, a positive sign of the species' reproduction in its sole habitat in the country. Surveys just a year ago had only identified deceased adults. Thanks to the Bumblebee Conservation Trust's diligent monitoring, efforts are in place to safeguard this beetle's ecosystem, emphasizing the vital need to protect its environment for lasting survival.

stories.title: North Carolina court backs review process after father demands $3,000 for children's overseas trips
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a North Carolina Court determined that a parenting coordinator has the authority to dictate travel regulations for divorced parents. This case highlighted conflicts regarding international trips with minors, driven by one parent's financial motivations rather than genuine safety worries. The decision underscores the importance of prioritizing children's welfare in travel arrangements, clarifying parental rights during custody disagreements in North Carolina.

stories.title: Arpita Singh, celebrated artist who painted real women, dies at 89
Harrison Ford and Calista Flockhart to Receive First Joint Philanthropy Award
Meet Indian-origin Anjali Sud, the new CEO of SiriusXM, succeeding Jennifer Witz
320 acres around 200-year-old North Carolina iron mine bought to protect five bat species
stories.summary: A former iron mine in North Carolina, which operated from the 1820s to the 1930s, now provides a winter shelter for five bat species, including rare and endangered ones. The Southern Appalachian Highlands Conservancy has purchased 320 acres around the historic mine to protect its underground tunnels, recovering forest and wildlife habitat. The move strengthens earlier conservation efforts to safeguard bats from habitat disturbance and white-nose syndrome, a deadly fungal disease.

stories.title: PM Modi speaks with Zelenskyy, discusses efforts for Russia-Ukraine peace deal
Blue Angels mystery deepens: Officer Daniell Cribb's profile disappears from Navy website after her mentor Scott Laux's dismissal
'I warned you before too': Kejriwal takes swipe at Yogi over SIR, congratulates Akhilesh in advance
'Why spend on R&D?' Rajeev Chandrasekhar mocks China's 'easier way' over Nvidia spy claim
stories.summary: Rajeev Chandrasekhar highlighted the recent honeytrapping allegations against Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang involving China. He criticised China's ethical standards in technology acquisition and alleged espionage practices. China responded by denying these allegations and labeling them as baseless. An independent investigation has been launched by Nvidia's board regarding the claims. Huang has also admitted to personal issues but maintains no national security breaches occurred.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Nvidia boss in Chinese spy scandal; Delhi's AQI turns severe; Iran's hidden oil network in China, and more
Gang posing as Army suppliers dupe Assam firm of Rs 11.5 crore, key accused held in Bengal
BJP's third-term bid, Congress's comeback hopes: What will decide Uttarakhand elections 2027?
Manipur census on hold till April 2027 as high court seeks answers from the Centre
stories.summary: The Manipur high court has ordered the postponement of the Census 2027 until late April 2027. This ruling aims to address significant concerns regarding how recent ethnic violence and subsequent displacements might skew population counts. The court requested the Census Commissioner to review seven representations. Following the authorities' decision, a further four-week delay will apply, allowing anyone unhappy with the outcome to seek legal recourse.

stories.title: Karnataka, Keralam governments launch E20 petrol quality checks amid ethanol blending concerns
stories.summary: The Keralam civil supplies department conducted inspections of petrol pumps in Kochi to examine the ethanol mix in E20 petrol. Officials took six samples, forwarding two for lab tests in Kakinada. Rising concerns over high ethanol blending have been highlighted by Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad. However, the union ministry of petroleum claims all samples adhere to quality norms, disputing allegations of excessive mixing.

stories.title: India, Lebanon hold first Foreign Office consultations; discuss trade, investment, digital cooperation
stories.summary: India and Lebanon embarked on their first-ever Foreign Office Consultations in New Delhi, aiming to strengthen their bilateral relationship. Important topics of discussion included cooperation in political-security, economic, and socio-cultural arenas. Ambassador Sripriya Ranganathan's visit to Lebanon set the stage for deeper ties, as key areas like trade, investment, digital infrastructure, and pharmaceuticals were reviewed, along with pressing regional and international matters.

stories.title: 'He called us Naxals': Rahul Gandhi hits back at PM Modi, renews debate challenge
'Semantically ignorant': Congress defends Kharge's 'Diwali a khushiyon ki Eid' remark
stories.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge stirred controversy by referring to Diwali as 'khushiyon ka Eid'. BJP officials accused the Congress of misrepresenting Diwali, asserting each festival has its unique identity. Pawan Khera of Congress defended Kharge's statement, emphasizing the meaning of 'Eid' as 'festival.' The BJP responded by questioning the appropriateness of comparing Diwali with Eid, which they deemed disrespectful. This disagreement highlights ongoing political tensions regarding religious and cultural identities.

stories.title: Delhi pollution sparks row: BJP alleges 'conspiracy'; AAP and Congress question AQI data
Jaishankar extends national day greetings to Cambodia, hails strong civilisational ties
stories.summary: S Jaishankar conveyed warm National Day wishes to Cambodia, celebrating the deep-rooted civilizational connections between the two countries. He praised the successful conclusion of the recent Cambodia-India Bilateral Army Exercise, CINBAX-II, which focused on collaborative training to bolster operational synergy among their armed forces. The exercise allowed both teams to display their professionalism and exchange valuable operational insights, further solidifying the defense partnership between India and Cambodia.

stories.title: Wisconsin family manages 500-acre forest for wildlife and timber; shortlisted for state conservation award
stories.summary: Jesse and Kylie Sebero are managing over 500 acres of forest in Marinette County, Wisconsin. They focus on timber production while ensuring ecological balance and wildlife conservation. The couple also opens their land for educational tours, helping others learn about forest management. They have been nominated for the 2026 Wisconsin Leopold Conservation Award for their significant contributions. The award will be announced during an upcoming meeting on November 12.

stories.title: South Carolina woman protects 146-acre family land after promise to mother
stories.summary: Alice Smith has placed her family's 146-acre property in South Carolina under a conservation easement, fulfilling a promise to her mother. Her grandparents bought the land in the 1940s. Along with another family, she has permanently restricted development on more than 250 acres through Upstate Forever.

stories.title: South Carolina father arrested after leaving 6-year-old alone for Pokemon cards
Princess Margaret's wedding gift: Mustique villa now rents for $50,000 a week
'True colours exposed': BJP's Giriraj Singh tears into Kharge over Diwali 'khushiyon ka Eid' remark
‘We’re losing a hell of a lot’: Cessna carrying 5 men vanished over Australia in 1981; 45 years later, no trace found
stories.summary: In August of 1981, a Cessna aircraft disappeared in Australia's Barrington Tops, carrying five men. Despite numerous searches and thorough investigations, both the plane and its passengers were never discovered. Reports indicated that severe turbulence and ice accumulation likely played a role in the incident. The mystery remains captivating for amateur sleuths and volunteers, while the families of the missing continue their quest for answers about their loved ones' fate.

stories.title: Doctors are using bacteria-killing viruses against superbugs that drugs cannot beat
stories.summary: Amidst the rising concern over antibiotic resistance, doctors are turning to phage therapy, a novel approach that employs viruses to target and eliminate dangerous bacteria. A recent Belgian study found that over 77% of patients showed significant clinical improvement. To enhance the application of personalized bacteriophage treatments, new international guidelines have been introduced, though researchers underline the importance of further studies to comprehend the therapy's potential fully.

stories.title: Ohio man keeps premarital home after divorce; wife ordered to pay $20,000 in legal fees
stories.summary: In a pivotal divorce ruling in Ohio, the court upheld the husband's ownership of his pre-marital property, rejecting the wife's assertions about marital contributions from their joint bank account. The trial court mandated that she pay $20,000 towards his legal expenses, reflecting on her actions throughout the proceedings. The husband's rental income was deemed adequate to maintain mortgage obligations, highlighting the relevance of asset tracking in such cases.

stories.title: Katy Perry and Russell Brand’s former estate rents for $275,000 monthly
High-Rise Fire Kills 14: Blaze rips through Taiyuan tower; authorities probe cause amid safety drive
stories.summary: On Sunday afternoon, a devastating fire erupted in a downtown high-rise building in Taiyuan, China. Firefighters responded swiftly, bringing the flames under control about two hours later, by 7 pm local time. The rescue efforts lasted until 8:30 pm, leading to the evacuation and hospitalization of 38 individuals. The unfortunate event initially reported five deaths, which later rose to 14 confirmed fatalities.

stories.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'
stories.summary: Sheikh Hasina has applied for a new passport and national identity card, indicating her intent to return and address the legal matters awaiting her in Bangladesh. Despite a prior ban, her Awami League party continues to enjoy robust support. Her return is likely to heighten the existing political unrest and may further complicate India-Bangladesh relations, as discussions on her extradition unfold.

stories.title: Chancellor Merz backs Ilse Aigner as Germany's first female President
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has endorsed Ilse Aigner for the upcoming presidential election in Germany. Aigner, if elected, would be the first woman to hold this position. Supported by the Christian Democratic Union and the Christian Social Union, she has backing from various political parties. She could succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier, whose presidency ends on March 18. Aigner has previous government experience and a strong political network in Germany.

stories.title: ‘Task Force Iron Gate in full force' to choke Iran's trade route, says Trump
stories.summary: Task Force Iron Gate is a new US initiative aimed at disrupting Iran's overland supply routes and preventing advanced weapons movement. It involves around 20 personnel coordinating with various US agencies from Tampa, Florida. The task force complements an existing naval blockade that has already hindered Iran's oil exports significantly. Humanitarian aid will remain exempt from these restrictions despite the new measures.

stories.title: 'Immigration policy too tough': 5 key takeaways from Trump's 60 minutes interview
stories.summary: Donald Trump admitted in a recent interview that the Iran war and deportation policies affected Republican midterm results. He acknowledged that while strong border security was supported, harsh deportation measures raised concerns among voters. Additionally, she founded Gorilla Conservation Coffee, which financially empowers farmers by promoting sustainable coffee farming while ensuring the protection of gorilla habitats, highlighting the necessity of teamwork in wildlife conservation and community development.

Syria rules out troop deployment to Yemen, says military ties with Saudi could expand
stories.summary: Syria has clarified that it will not deploy troops to Yemen despite previous reports suggesting otherwise. A diplomatic source stated that military cooperation with Saudi Arabia is anticipated to deepen in the future. Saudi Arabia is currently facing tensions with the Houthi rebels and seeks military assistance from various allies. Syria and Saudi Arabia recently signed a defense cooperation agreement as ties between the countries strengthen.

stories.title: Brooklyn tenants faced a $120,000 claim after renting from a fake owner; court later dismissed it after a sale
stories.summary: In a perplexing turn of events, Deborah and Demetris Jones rented an apartment under the false pretense of ownership in Brooklyn. Legal complications followed as the courts ruled the original landlord could no longer enforce tenancy agreements after selling the property. A subsequent settlement with the new owner granted the tenants temporary residence, illuminating significant considerations for tenants during changes in property ownership.

stories.title: Dundee manager fired over £21,360 pothole repairs wins £34,326 compensation
stories.summary: A Dundee transport manager who worked for a furniture company for over 24 years was dismissed after it questioned £21,360 in pothole repair bills. A tribunal found that the company had failed to investigate the matter fairly, overlooked findings that cleared him of wrongdoing and wrongly dismissed him. It ordered the company to pay him £34,326.

stories.title: North Carolina student wins $2M, thanks to gas pump glitch
stories.summary: Bram Dunehew, a college student, experienced a life-changing moment when a gas pump malfunction led him to purchase a $2 million Powerball ticket. While waiting for his receipt at a convenience store, he decided on a whim to join the lottery. Dunehew matched all five white balls during the Halloween night drawing.

stories.title: Canadian landowners donated property worth more than C$2 million
stories.summary: In a remarkable partnership, Ducks Unlimited Canada has safeguarded over 1,100 acres in southern Quebec, thanks to more than C$2 million in funding from local landowners. This significant conservation effort is vital for maintaining ecological balance and biodiversity, while a newly opened 1.5-kilometre trail enhances public access to these precious habitats.

stories.title: Zelenskyy says Russia hit Ukrainian energy facility with North Korean KN-23 missiles
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia is using North Korean KN-23 missiles against Ukraine. He emphasized the need for stronger global sanctions against countries supplying military assistance. Zelenskyy noted a critical shortage of US-made Patriot missile interceptors affecting Ukraine's defense capabilities. Russia's intensified attacks are exacerbating the situation as winter approaches. Military cooperation between North Korea and Russia has significantly increased in recent months.

stories.title: 'Need matured LoP': Kiren Rijiju offers 'friendly advice' to Congress
Indian-American Priya Sundareshan elected Arizona Senate president as Democrats secure historic state control
Wrexham Kop Stand Expansion: planners clear 7,750-seat upgrade; capacity tops 18,000
stories.summary: The planning authority has given Wrexham AFC the go-ahead to increase the capacity of the new Kop Stand to 7,750 seats, enhancing the Racecourse Ground's venue status for major global events, such as international football. Work began on the stand in December 2025 and is set for completion by early 2027.

stories.title: Woman’s niece discovers 1930 painting hidden for decades in New York apartment; artwork bought for $3,800 could fetch $3 million at auction
stories.summary: Georgia O’Keeffe’s long-lost artwork, 'Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I', is set to make waves at an upcoming auction. After nearly 40 years hidden in a New York apartment closet, the painting resurfaced thanks to a spontaneous mention by the niece of its original owner. It will be showcased to the public before its auction on November 17, 2026, with proceeds aimed at supporting family projects and educational initiatives.

stories.title: Did Abdul El-Sayed get his Wikipedia page edited to soften controversial sentences before Michigan Senate election? Larry Sanger responds
Trump admin drops lawsuit seeking to block 20,000 California ballots
Idaho hunters kill 12 newborn wolf pups in a single day
stories.summary: Three hunters in Idaho killed 12 wolf pups, receiving up to $2,000 for each animal. The state’s programme reimburses hunters, raising concerns over the use of taxpayer money. Critics have condemned these actions as a form of bounty hunting, especially targeting newborn pups. Wildlife experts have expressed concerns about the method of killings and potential effects on wolf populations.

stories.title: Cyndi Lauper, Ariana DeBose help New York charity gala raise over $750,000 for nonprofits
stories.summary: At the 2026 Fetch Pet Gala in New York City, stars like Cyndi Lauper and Ariana DeBose brought their talents to the stage, raising over $750,000 for four animal rescue nonprofits. This event also featured adoptable dogs gracing a green carpet, enhancing their chances for adoption. SATELLAI, the event's sponsor, contributed by providing devices to new pet adopters, showcasing a powerful community commitment to animal welfare through celebrity support.

stories.title: 'Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented damage': Sonia Gandhi on Emergency
‘She wanted a traditional ceremony’: DMK leader responds to criticism over Vedic rituals at granddaughter’s wedding
Why can't Congress break free from Gandhi family? Sonia responds to nepotism charge
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi addressed questions about her family's leadership of the Congress party during an interview. She downplayed allegations of nepotism while asserting the party's potential to challenge the BJP. Gandhi reflected on her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi's Emergency decision and described it as a mistake. She recounted personal trauma from losing both Indira and her husband Rajiv Gandhi to assassinations.

stories.title: Hands-on inspection: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw buys tea via UPI, interacts with passengers at Anand Vihar Station
stories.summary: Passengers shared positive feedback regarding ongoing facility upgrades, cleanliness, and waiting area enhancements implemented by Indian Railways.

stories.title: Nazi spies landed on US soil days before German U-boat sank Canadian ship off Maine in 1944; 82 years later, divers find wreck 400 feet underwater
stories.summary: Divers from the Nomad Exploration Team located the wreck of the SS Cornwallis nearly 400 feet underwater. This ship was torpedoed by a German submarine in December 1944, resulting in the deaths of 43 crew members. The submarine also secretly landed two Nazi spies on the coast of Maine just days before. The discovery highlights an important historical event involving espionage during World War II.

stories.title: UK bride dances with hospitalised dad: she brings wedding to his ward; staff help arrange the dance
stories.summary: Sinead Jackson's wedding was uniquely touched by bittersweet circumstances as her father, Leslie Healy, was hospitalized only days before the event. Hospital personnel facilitated a heartwarming moment, allowing Sinead to don her wedding dress for a dance with her father. Though Leslie couldn't physically attend, technology enabled him to witness the ceremony.

stories.title: West Bengal SIR: Fourth retired judge resigns from appeals tribunals, cites ‘personal reasons’
'First apologise to devotees, saints': UP CM Yogi ahead of Akhilesh Yadav's Ram Temple visit
Florida court rules legal-fees clause cannot automatically bind future owners after $40,000 trespass award
stories.summary: A recent ruling by the Florida Supreme Court clarified that attorney-fees clauses do not automatically apply to future property owners. The case originated with an easement agreement involving Crown Castle South LLC and RJ's International Trading LLC. Although RJ's secured damages for trespass, it sought attorney fees based on the original agreement. The court determined that the legal-fees clause lacked connection to the use or enjoyment of the land.

New York founder turned 1,000 cancelled meals into a food initiative that has donated 4 million
stories.summary: The Migrant Kitchen was born from a cancelled catering order amidst the COVID-19 crisis, initially providing meals to healthcare workers. Over time, it evolved to tackle food insecurity by serving thousands of meals daily to marginalized communities, emphasizing culturally relevant dishes. Employing around 100 individuals, mostly immigrants, it mirrors the community it supports and has expanded its reach beyond New York City into Philadelphia, enhancing emergency meal delivery efforts.

stories.title: In 1935, a Black linguist recorded Louisiana Creole speakers on aluminium discs
stories.summary: Research into recordings made in 1935 is shedding light on the vital voices of Louisiana Creole and Louisiana French speakers. Linguist Lorenzo Dow Turner's findings reveal significant aspects of the language and its vibrant cultural ties within Black communities. Dr. Oliver Mayeux's work revived these gems, showcasing unique grammatical features and vocabulary. As the cultural importance of Louisiana Creole is recognized, initiatives are fostering language revival efforts across the region.

stories.title: Data protection law faces scrutiny: The key concerns explained
Diljit Dosanjh barred from singing ‘Patiala Peg’, 3 other songs at Indore concert amid child safety concerns
stories.summary: Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh faces a ban on performing four songs during his upcoming concert in Indore. Authorities cited worries over the songs' promotion of liquor and violence, especially regarding children's impact. The District Child Protection Officer received a complaint highlighting these concerns and the guidelines from the Punjab and Haryana High Court. Additionally, restrictions include limitations on children on stage and the singer's costume.

stories.title: 'Ask Karnataka to seek consent of co-basin states': Tamil Nadu CM Vijay urges PM Modi over Mekedatu dam project
Ayodhya glows with 30 lakh diyas as Deepotsav lights up Saryu ghats on Diwali eve
stories.summary: Lakhs of diyas illuminated Ram Ki Paidi ghat, while more than 30 lakh earthen lamps were set to light up 56 ghats along the river, turning the temple town into a spectacular sea of lights. The annual celebration, which marks return of Lord Ram to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana, recreates the traditional welcome believed to have been given to him by the people of the city in the Treta Yuga.

stories.title: Nikki Haley's analysis of GOP's midterm loss: 'You can't blame media, academia, Hollywood'; Son Nalin Haley agrees

100 days adrift in the Pacific Ocean: Nine leave Micronesia by boat; 5 survive, 4 die in Kiribati
stories.summary: Nine family members from Micronesia set out on what was supposed to be a one-hour boat journey to collect supplies. A storm swept their vessel off course, leaving them adrift in the Pacific Ocean for nearly 100 days. They eventually reached Kiribati, more than 3,000 miles away, but only five survived the ordeal.

stories.title: How much does the British Royal Family cost taxpayers? King Charles' £137.9m grant, William's wealth
stories.summary: The British Royal Family receives £137.9 million through the Sovereign Grant in 2026/27, but a new bill proposes reducing the funding to £99.9 million the following year. Meanwhile, reports reveal Prince William’s £1.2 billion Duchy of Cornwall valuation and King Charles’ estimated £640 million fortune, raising questions about royal wealth, income and taxes.

stories.title: Penguin was 'uneasy' with criticism of govt: Sonia Gandhi's 1st reaction to memoir row
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi voiced her dismay over Penguin Random House India's decision to withdraw her memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', due to disagreements about sensitive subjects involving Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She interpreted this as an effort to inhibit her narrative and suggested possible government influence.

‘Grow up, Pramila’: Harmeet Dhillon hits back at Democrat leader Jayapal over ‘knitting’ jibe after DOJ exit
Iran ramps up threats against US, removes cap on ballistic missile range
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the removal of missile range restrictions while preparing for asymmetric warfare. This statement follows limited US strikes targeting Iranian anti-aircraft systems in the region. Reports indicated that explosions in Qeshm Island were due to Iranian air defense exercises and not hostile actions. US officials claim the Iranian air defense systems were severely weakened during previous conflicts.

stories.title: Army debunks Pakistan propaganda about 'Chinese troops inside Arunachal'
stories.summary: The Indian Army has strongly refuted false reports on social media suggesting that Chinese forces made significant territorial gains in Arunachal Pradesh. Claims of a 50 km advance in early November were thoroughly investigated, revealing six accounts deliberately pushing misleading information. Official sources assure that there has been no major defeat of Indian troops, emphasizing the importance of relying on credible sources for updates on border issues to combat misinformation.

Florida court upholds wife's protection order after husband turns up unannounced over Ferrari
stories.summary: A Florida appeals court upheld a domestic violence protection order against a husband who visited his estranged wife's condo asking about his Ferrari. Although video evidence did not support her account of the visit, three earlier incidents of physical violence provided grounds for the order.

stories.title: Meet Pooja Verma, who built bird boxes that photograph nesting birds every three minutes
stories.summary: California student Pooja Verma has won first place in the 36th ‘A Voice for Animals’ contest for developing solar-powered bird boxes with cameras that photograph nesting birds every three minutes. Her nonprofit, Eco Innovate, has distributed the boxes to 10 schools and plans to expand the project across California and the US.

stories.summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh shared a video showcasing Indian Air Force personnel singing a patriotic song. He praised their musical talent, stating it reflects their dedication to serving the country. Singh emphasized the importance of remaining vigilant against evolving national security threats and misinformation. He addressed air warriors at Bagdogra Air Force Station, highlighting the need for operational readiness in modern warfare.

Earth has a new mini-moon: Tiny asteroid 2026 QQ8 was captured in April, spotted in August and will leave by early 2027
stories.summary: A minor asteroid, known as 2026 QQ8, found its way into Earth's gravity in April 2026. Observed for the first time in August, astronomers identified it as a natural celestial body. This mini-moon will remain within our orbit for approximately eight to nine months before departing. Its nearest approach is calculated to be 568,000 kilometers away, carrying no threat of impact as it joins the transient mini-moon collection around Earth.

stories.title: Malaysia's king warns against challenging Najib Razak's house-arrest pardon after $12 million fine paid
stories.summary: Sultan Ibrahim of Malaysia has cautioned against any attempts to contest the conditional pardon granted to Najib Razak for house arrest. The process of Najib's transfer from prison has stalled as authorities seek legal clarification on the pardon’s implications. The attorney-general emphasized that the goal is merely to address legal uncertainties, not to challenge the King's directive.

stories.title: ‘My family, I face threat’: Italy minister says his private data leaked on dark web
stories.summary: Antonio Tajani, Italy's foreign minister, revealed that his personal information is being circulated by cybercriminals on the dark web. This alarming situation has led to threats against him and his family. Tajani indicated these criminals are seeking more personal details. However, he remains resolute in enhancing security collaboration and reaffirmed Italy's steadfast support for Ukraine despite these ongoing threats.

TikTok accused of becoming a gateway to the online sex industry for young girls
stories.summary: TikTok faces accusations of inadvertently promoting an online sex industry targeting young women and girls. Recent research highlights how popular OnlyFans creators use subtle cues in TikTok videos. These performers appear to endorse financial independence through selling adult content while circumventing platform restrictions. Additionally, TikTok's algorithm contributes to the circulation of these videos among teenagers. Advocates call for stricter regulations to protect minors from adult content influences across social media.

stories.title: Utah millionaire father of seven built a 300-acre doomsday compound stocked with food, weapons and supplies to shelter 200 people if civilisation collapses
stories.summary: Jayson Orvis has created a 300-acre doomsday sanctuary in the heart of Utah, designed to accommodate 200 people during catastrophic circumstances. This unique compound showcases greenhouses and a flourishing food forest, underpinning his vision of cooperative survival. While Orvis maintains a level of skepticism about imminent apocalypse risks, he acknowledges the importance of community over solitude in potential crises.

stories.title: Texas court upholds refinery's gross negligence in worker's death, cuts award by $125,000
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court upheld a refinery company's gross negligence in a worker's asbestos-related death but reduced his family's damages award from $325,000 to $200,000. It also revived negligence claims that had earlier been dismissed, allowing the family to pursue them in further proceedings.

stories.summary: A Dutch man who lost his wedding ring while threshing grain in 1942 or 1943 has had it returned to his family 83 years later. A metal detector user found it buried 20 centimetres underground in Odiliapeel and personally returned it to the owner's son, Bert Nabuurs, refusing a reward. The ring's engraved wedding date confirmed its identity.

stories.title: ‘Relief to breathe Kerala’s clean air’: Shashi Tharoor takes swipe at Delhi govt over pollution crisis
'Democratic rights were curtailed but constitutionally': Sonia Gandhi reflects on Emergency
Als Nursing Hospital Opens: 14-year ALS drive builds specialised facility; 350,000 donors fund care
stories.summary: In March 2025, the Seungil Hope Nursing Hospital in Yongin welcomed its first ALS patients, marking a 14-year journey led by dedicated advocates Park Seung-il and Sean. This landmark facility, developed with the generosity of over 350,000 donors and government backing, aims to provide advanced care tailored to the unique needs of those with ALS, emphasizing a community's unwavering commitment to enhancing the lives of affected individuals.

‘E20 turned into 420’: Rahul Gandhi alleges petrol samples from Karnataka exceed 20% ethanol limit
Republicans spent more, Democrats won more: Inside the costliest US midterm battle
stories.summary: In the 2026 US midterm elections, Democrats made notable gains among Latino voters, following a period of prior support for Republicans. Increased spending by GOP candidates did not secure the anticipated wins, resulting in losses in key districts. High turnout from Latino constituents significantly impacted voting dynamics nationwide, with many responding negatively to proposed data centre projects.

France deploys 70,000 security personnel ahead of fresh nationwide protests
stories.summary: French trade unions and student groups are organizing a day of protests against rising living costs. The Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris, despite an official ban on gatherings. Nationwide demonstrations have been ongoing for weeks, with participants demanding wage increases and better conditions for youth. On Monday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu will meet with union representatives to discuss these issues.

stories.title: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme
stories.summary: The United States has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information regarding Iran's nuclear program. This reward aims to gather details about facilities, equipment, and personnel involved with the program. Diplomatic efforts are ongoing to resolve tensions and prevent further conflict. Iran has expressed the desire for negotiations but requires certain conditions to be met.

stories.title: US-China trade talks to continue as Washington presses Beijing to honour Busan deal
stories.summary: China and the US are engaged in ongoing dialogues to foster stable trade relations, with emphasis on prior commitments. US officials expressed concern regarding China's adherence to agreements related to rare earth materials and agricultural products. The latest discussions revealed the US's stance that China falls short in fulfilling its responsibilities under the Busan agreement. Moreover, China dismissed accusations of inadequate rare earth supplies and agricultural purchasing.

'Voices in head said to kill Trump': Man with firearms and ammunition arrested near White House
stories.summary: The Secret Service took Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos into custody after he exhibited alarming conduct in his vehicle. When confronted by officers, he insisted that he heard voices commanding him to execute President Trump. A subsequent search of his stolen car revealed three guns and additional ammunition. A Venezuelan national without legal status since March 2024, Chrinos now underscores the persistent dangers faced by the president.

'Dallas' star Victoria Principal, 76, now rescues animals on her ranch; shares miniature horse Halo's recovery
stories.summary: Former actress Victoria Principal has found her true calling in animal rehabilitation, dedicating her life to caring for rescued creatures at her ranch. One notable resident is Halo, a miniature horse currently healing with her support. Principal passionately advocates for the role of love and patience in nurturing these animals back to health, marking a significant departure from her Hollywood days as she embraces her new purpose.

'Jackass' star Steve-O turns 44-acre Tennessee ranch into a home for rescued animals
stories.summary: Steve-O, the famous Jackass star, has dedicated himself to animal welfare by establishing The Radical Ranch, a sanctuary for rescued animals situated near Nashville. Since its inception as a nonprofit in 2024, the ranch has provided a home for nine animals, including goats and pigs. Steve-O envisions expanding the sanctuary to include cows and chickens while fostering empathy towards all creatures.

Manipur rebel arrested from Delhi hotel
In 2017, Gaten Matarazzo helped form a charity; nine years later, its partners issued 37 care tips
stories.summary: Cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD) affects bone and dental development in patients and requires specialized care. A recent study established 37 expert recommendations for diagnosing and managing this rare condition effectively. These guidelines emphasize the importance of coordinated care among various specialists and regular monitoring. Gaten Matarazzo, who has CCD, advocates for better recognition and treatment of the disorder. CCD Smiles organization aims to support patients through awareness and research initiatives.

California condo parking dispute ends after decade; court rejects $292,544 legal fee claim
stories.summary: In a contentious parking dispute in Orange County, condominium owners WCST Enterprises and Berit Ling faced off in court. Ultimately, the court ruled in favor of WCST, affirming its claim to garage space 38G-a. However, despite the legal victory, WCST could not reclaim its substantial legal fees of $292,544, as these claims did not meet California statutes for fee recovery.

stories.title: 125-year-old Idaho ranch gets permanent protection
stories.summary: A conservation easement has been established on the Flying A Ranch in Idaho to protect the land. This easement allows the Atchley family to continue their farming operations while preventing future development. The agreement also supports a crucial wildlife migration corridor for mule deer and various other species. Previous efforts to protect the ranch were led by Clen Atchley, who passed away in 2024.

HC judge vacancies at decade-low 26%, but pendency keeps piling up
NMC adds 9,783 PG medical seats, takes total to 68,305
New research rules out the theory of Stonehenge Altar Stone's Northeast Scottish Origin
stories.summary: Researchers continue to explore the origins of the Altar Stone at Stonehenge, which weighs approximately six tonnes. Recent studies suggested a possible origin from northeast Scotland, but findings have complicated this theory. A new international team's research found no matching source from the Scottish locations they examined, narrowing possibilities down. Previous assumptions about the Altar Stone's Welsh origins have been challenged by new geological insights.

stories.title: Brisbane Library House Auction: former private library cleared for sale; rebuild interest grows
stories.summary: After years of neglect, a three-bedroom home in Wynnum, Brisbane, has undergone a remarkable transformation. This property, once filled with a vast collection of books and memorabilia, required extensive teamwork to clear out its contents and evict wildlife. Now, it's being showcased as an exciting renovation or rebuilding opportunity in a sought-after neighborhood, with an auction date set for November 14, 2026, drawing potential buyers eager to invest.

Ousted Videocon promoter Dhoot declared bankrupt over dues worth Rs 12,668cr

Louisiana woman fights uncle over mother's estate for 13 years; court revives part of lawsuit
stories.summary: A Louisiana woman accused her uncle of transferring interests in nearly 300 acres of her late mother's estate to himself and businesses linked to him. More than 23 years after her mother's death, an appeals court revived her claims concerning his handling of the estate but upheld the dismissal of other claims. It also cancelled a $10,000 damages award and ordered further proceedings.

stories.title: For more than 60 years, visitors walked through a cave in Spain; now 280 motifs identified
stories.summary: A remarkable archaeological find at Cova de la Font Major has revealed 280 Palaeolithic engravings, showcasing diverse motifs of animals and geometric shapes. This challenges the previously held notion that cave art was scarce in northeastern Iberia, where only two pieces were known. These engravings suggest the existence of unique artistic traditions independent of the famous Franco-Cantabrian region, offering new insights into the cultural practices of Ice Age Europe.

stories.title: Twenty black grouse were moved from the North Pennines to the North York Moors in 2024
stories.summary: In a remarkable conservation achievement, black grouse have successfully hatched chicks in North York Moors after a long absence of 200 years. In 2024, 20 black grouse were moved from North Pennines as part of a dedicated effort that includes habitat restoration and management of predators. Reports indicate a notable rise in the number of displaying males, with plans for further translocations underway to bolster their population even more.

stories.title: ‘Mad Men’ star John Slattery joins Ocean Conservancy campaign to protect oceans
North Carolina student wins top award for free tool mapping wildlife roadkill hotspots
stories.summary: Aaryan Ghorpade, a North Carolina student, has triumphed in a national competition with EcoRoute, a project that tracks wildlife-vehicle collision hotspots across the U.S. This innovative online tool gathers collision data and produces heat maps to assist transportation agencies in improving road safety. EcoRoute also encourages community involvement, allowing users to report wildlife sightings. Ghorpade envisions further enhancements and plans to partner with wildlife conservation organizations in his state.

stories.title: Indian family seeks help to bring back man's body after he dies from burn injuries in New Zealand on birthday
Stephen King's Maine mansion becomes a literary archive, with $2,500 writers' retreats next door
stories.summary: Stephen King and Tabitha have innovatively turned their Bangor residence into a unique archive and retreat for writers. This initiative offers aid and an inspiring atmosphere, allowing selected authors to immerse themselves in their work. The nearby Brown Mansion will serve as an additional haven, benefitting a variety of literary talents, including educators and Maine local writers.

stories.title: Streamer Feud Over Halloween: Banks slams Plaqueboymax’s ‘whiteface’ stream; questions career slide
stories.summary: Plaqueboymax’s Halloween livestream led to disagreements with Adin Ross and FaZe Banks. Adin suggested a blackface stream after seeing Max’s crew dressed as stereotypical white men. Max questioned Adin’s respect for Black culture, while Banks said Max’s costume showed disrespect towards white people. Banks also criticised Max’s content, career direction and Super Bowl halftime show ambitions, and invoked Kai Cenat.

What led to Susie Wiles' firing within 3 days of Trump's midterm loss? 'Ice maiden' was Trump's longest serving chief of staff
stories.summary: Susie Wiles fired: Within three days of midterm rout, President Donald Trump elevated Stephen Miller to the post of Chief of Staff replacing Susie Wiles, who served the longest on the post. The decision was not out of the blue as there were speculations which the president at that time dismissed.

stories.summary: Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams from Sacred Heart Preparatory have pioneered an Advanced Placement course focused on women's history, garnering endorsement from 100 esteemed universities and colleges. This initiative underscores the vital role women have played throughout history. An eminent gala in Chicago on November 6, 2026, will unveil the inaugural Meryl Streep Educator Award, with proceeds dedicated to bolstering educational resources for women's history.

stories.title: India’s only floating post office gets longer working hours
Will you comply with Japanese laws? Japan plans new question for foreign visitors on entry form
US mother transfers property to son in 2003; court cancels deed after he refuses to return it
stories.summary: A New York mother who transferred her property to her son and daughter-in-law in 2003 after he promised to return it whenever asked has won a legal battle 23 years later. When the couple refused to return the property, she approached the court. A New York appeals court has now upheld the cancellation of the deed, ruling in her favour.

stories.title: London councillors reject Berkeley Homes plan after affordable housing offer falls from 40% to 12%
stories.summary: Southwark Council's planning committee voted unanimously against Berkeley Homes' revised plans for the Bermondsey Place development. The housebuilder proposed reducing affordable housing from 40 percent to just 12 percent, causing strong local opposition. Council members expressed concerns about the long timeline for home completion and questioned the developer's financial figures. Berkeley Homes highlighted rising costs and council fees as reasons for the reduced affordable housing offer.

stories.title: Court upholds sale of divorced Arkansas woman's property share after her bankruptcy filing.
stories.summary: In a landmark ruling, a federal appeals court upheld the sale of a divorced woman's stake in property located in Arkansas. The decision favored her bankruptcy trustee, overcoming objections posed by her ex-husband. He contended that the buyer's good faith was not adequately proven in prior hearings but failed to voice this concern earlier. Consequently, the property transaction with Blue Sun Capital LLC is deemed legally binding.

stories.title: '100% in favour': Trump backs AI expansion despite growing data centre backlash
‘Breaking Bad’ star Dean Norris lists California ranch for $3.2 million amid divorce and bankruptcy proceedings
stories.summary: Dean Norris has listed his expansive 11-acre ranch in Temecula for an asking price of $3,199,267 amidst ongoing divorce proceedings. His wife, Bridget, filed for divorce due to irreconcilable differences, while also pursuing joint custody of their children. Compounding their challenges, the couple's restaurant, Swing Inn Cafe, has entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Featuring an infinity pool and horse barn, the ranch attracts potential buyers seeking luxury.

stories.title: Indian student Sreeja Koya Reddy missing in Boston for 3 days; police seek public's help to trace 23-year-old
Show Hope marks 10,000 adoptions across 65 countries, surpassing its founders' original goal
stories.summary: Show Hope, the non-profit organization founded by Steven Curtis Chapman and Mary Beth in 2003, has achieved significant milestones. The charity has successfully helped over 10,000 children find permanent families through its adoption grants. In celebration of this achievement, a benefit concert will be held at the Grand Ole Opry featuring notable artists. Five dollars from each ticket sold will support the organization's ongoing programs.

stories.title: 'Convince Modi ji for SIR debate': Rahul Gandhi tells Amit Shah to stop confusing PM, shares video of remarks
PM Modi's Sule message to Sharad Pawar; 'internal tussle' in NCP: Is Maharashtra politics heading for another churn?

A meeting of senior NCP leaders with Union home minister Amit Shah amid reports of discontent within the party has fuelled speculations. NCP chief Sunetra Pawar has convened meetings to address unity concerns after Ajit Pawar's death. Rohit Pawar has issued a caution to the family regaridng possible BJP manoeuvres.

stories.title: 16 Canadians moved to Florida in 2022 on instruction of cult leader Liana Shanti. After years of legal battle, 3 get $56 million in defamation case
3M agrees to pay up to $7.35 billion in PFAS water contamination settlement involving 120,000 people
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, 3M has agreed to a $7.35 billion resolution for personal injury claims linked to PFAS exposure. This crucial settlement is designed to aid individuals asserting health damages from polluted water and products. The claims process is set up to fairly assess and settle cases expeditiously, with around 120,000 potential beneficiaries meeting defined eligibility criteria. This agreement marks a pivotal move toward tackling PFAS-related health problems.

stories.title: 'Directed at Delhi govt officials': Court dismisses plea seeking FIR against CM Rekha Gupta over Lord Hanuman remark
1983 Air Canada jet runs out of fuel mid-air, but pilots land safely with all 69 aboard
stories.summary: On July 23, 1983, an Air Canada Boeing 767 experienced a loss of engine power while traversing over Manitoba. With 61 passengers and 8 crew aboard, a serious fuel miscalculation by ground staff resulted in a 45 percent shortage. Remarkably, the pilots managed to glide the aircraft and executed an emergency landing on an old military track. Thankfully, everyone onboard suffered only minor injuries, and the plane was later restored.

stories.title: Michael Jordans's Wings initiative supports 4,000 scholars, awards 350 in 2025

Notary rewrites 88-year-old woman’s will to inherit her fortune
stories.summary: In a shocking case from Braunfels, an 88-year-old woman’s intention to leave her estate to charities was thwarted by a corrupt former notary who forged her will. The Limburg Regional Court imposed a two-year suspended sentence on the notary, who attributed his actions to financial stress but was ultimately deemed to have acted out of greed. His courtroom apology raises questions about the potential repercussions for the woman’s family.

stories.title: Living near a highway toll plaza? New FASTag rule offers annual pass of up to Rs 3,000, but there's a catch
stories.summary: Residents living within 20 km of National Highway toll plazas can apply for a Concessional Local Pass. The pass costs Rs 1,500 or Rs 3,000 annually, depending on the plaza's location. To qualify, motorists must have a functional FASTag, and their vehicle must be non-commercial. The scheme aims to reduce toll expenses for eligible residents but has specific restrictions.

stories.title: Trump had demanded that Harmeet K Dhillon be fired after he watched her on 60 Minutes on October 18: Report
North Carolina court revives roofing firm's lawsuits against insurers over unpaid storm repairs
stories.summary: A North Carolina appeals court has reinstated lawsuits from Piedmont Roofing Services against various major insurance companies. Overturning an earlier trial judge's dismissal of breach of contract claims, the court concluded that sufficient grounds exist for the roofing company to pursue its claims. This ruling sheds light on the intricate legal issues related to the transfer of insurance rights in property damage situations.

stories.title: Evening Newswrap: Panic as Karmabhoomi Express catches fire in Punjab; bomb threats to Bombay HC, BSE and Amitabh Bachchan’s residence, and more

Eva Longoria-backed charity supports 100+ children at Vietnam orphanage, expands plans to Spain therapy centre
stories.summary: Since 2018, the Global Gift Foundation has championed the Quang Chau Orphanage, now known as Casa Ángeles, providing care to over 100 needy children. This initiative, bolstered by funds from the Global Gift Gala in Paris, also supports the Casa Ángeles therapy centre in Spain. Through engaging performances and a vibrant auction, the event helps sustain vital projects aimed at uplifting vulnerable communities.

stories.title: At 9, she started feeding hungry children; now her nonprofit has reached over 110,000 people
stories.summary: New Jersey teenager Anakh Sawhney started Rice Kids in 2018, aged nine, to provide meals to hungry children. Her nonprofit has since supported more than 110,000 people across five US states and parts of India through food, education, healthcare and other essential resources. More than half of the students supported by the organisation in India have returned to mainstream education.

Michigan brother ploughs landscaped strip beside sibling's home, triggering bitter land dispute
stories.summary: A Michigan appeals court revived a couple's claim over a 0.13-acre strip allegedly landscaped by their family for years. The dispute began after the husband's brother ploughed the land in 2022. The court ruled that a 1991 foreclosure judgment did not prevent the boundary claim, while leaving the $5,364.44 award for trespass and waste undisturbed.

stories.title: New York buyer loses $1 million lawsuit after demanding $270,000 cut on $550,000 Bronx home deal
stories.summary: A man from New York made a cash offer for a dilapidated home in the Bronx, agreeing to accept it in its current state. After finding additional issues just days before the closing, he sought a considerable price decrease. The seller declined, referring to the contract terms and previous property condition disclosures.
